paragraphs.text: Jesus therefore six days before the passover came to Bethany, where Lazarus was, whom Jesus raised from the dead.
paragraphs.original: Ὁ οὖν Ἰησοῦς πρὸ ἓξ ἡμερῶν τοῦ πάσχα ἦλθεν εἰς Βηθανίαν, ὅπου ἦν Λάζαρος, ὃν ἤγειρεν ἐκ νεκρῶν Ἰησοῦς.
paragraphs.translit: Ho oun Iēsous pro hex hēmerōn tou pascha ēlthen eis Bēthanian, hopou ēn Lazaros, hon ēgeiren ek nekrōn Iēsous.

paragraphs.text: So they made him a supper there: and Martha served; but Lazarus was one of them that sat at meat with him.
paragraphs.original: ἐποίησαν οὖν αὐτῷ δεῖπνον ἐκεῖ, καὶ ἡ Μάρθα διηκόνει, ὁ δὲ Λάζαρος εἷς ἦν ἐκ τῶν ἀνακειμένων σὺν αὐτῷ·
paragraphs.translit: epoiēsan oun autō deipnon ekei, kai hē Martha diēkonei, ho de Lazaros heis ēn ek tōn anakeimenōn syn autō·

paragraphs.text: Mary therefore took a pound of ointment of pure nard, very precious, and anointed the feet of Jesus, and wiped his feet with her hair: and the house was filled with the odor of the ointment.
paragraphs.original: ἡ οὖν Μαριὰμ λαβοῦσα λίτραν μύρου νάρδου πιστικῆς πολυτίμου ἤλειψεν τοὺς πόδας τοῦ Ἰησοῦ καὶ ἐξέμαξεν ταῖς θριξὶν αὐτῆς τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ· ἡ δὲ οἰκία ἐπληρώθη ἐκ τῆς ὀσμῆς τοῦ μύρου.
paragraphs.translit: hē oun Mariam labousa litran myrou nardou pistikēs polytimou ēleipsen tous podas tou Iēsou kai exemaxen tais thrixin autēs tous podas autou· hē de oikia eplērōthē ek tēs osmēs tou myrou.

paragraphs.text: But Judas Iscariot, one of his disciples, that should betray him, saith,
paragraphs.original: λέγει δὲ Ἰούδας ὁ Ἰσκαριώτης εἷς τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ, ὁ μέλλων αὐτὸν παραδιδόναι·
paragraphs.translit: legei de Ioudas ho Iskariōtēs heis tōn mathētōn autou, ho mellōn auton paradidonai·

paragraphs.text: Why was not this ointment sold for three hundred shillings, and given to the poor?
paragraphs.original: Διὰ τί τοῦτο τὸ μύρον οὐκ ἐπράθη τριακοσίων δηναρίων καὶ ἐδόθη πτωχοῖς;
paragraphs.translit: Dia ti touto to myron ouk eprathē triakosiōn dēnariōn kai edothē ptōchois;

paragraphs.text: Now this he said, not because he cared for the poor; but because he was a thief, and having the bag took away what was put therein.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ τοῦτο οὐχ ὅτι περὶ τῶν πτωχῶν ἔμελεν αὐτῷ, ἀλλʼ ὅτι κλέπτης ἦν καὶ τὸ γλωσσόκομον ἔχων τὰ βαλλόμενα ἐβάσταζεν.
paragraphs.translit: eipen de touto ouch hoti peri tōn ptōchōn emelen autō, allʼ hoti kleptēs ēn kai to glōssokomon echōn ta ballomena ebastazen.

paragraphs.text: Jesus therefore said, Suffer her to keep it against the day of my burying.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἄφες αὐτήν, ἵνα εἰς τὴν ἡμέραν τοῦ ἐνταφιασμοῦ μου τηρήσῃ αὐτό·
paragraphs.translit: eipen oun ho Iēsous· Aphes autēn, hina eis tēn hēmeran tou entaphiasmou mou tērēsē auto·

paragraphs.text: For the poor ye have always with you; but me ye have not always.
paragraphs.original: τοὺς πτωχοὺς γὰρ πάντοτε ἔχετε μεθʼ ἑαυτῶν, ἐμὲ δὲ οὐ πάντοτε ἔχετε.
paragraphs.translit: tous ptōchous gar pantote echete methʼ heautōn, eme de ou pantote echete.

paragraphs.text: The common people therefore of the Jews learned that he was there: and they came, not for Jesus` sake only, but that they might see Lazarus also, whom he had raised from the dead.
paragraphs.original: Ἔγνω οὖν ὄχλος πολὺς ἐκ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ὅτι ἐκεῖ ἐστιν, καὶ ἦλθον οὐ διὰ τὸν Ἰησοῦν μόνον, ἀλλʼ ἵνα καὶ τὸν Λάζαρον ἴδωσιν ὃν ἤγειρεν ἐκ νεκρῶν.
paragraphs.translit: Egnō oun ochlos polys ek tōn Ioudaiōn hoti ekei estin, kai ēlthon ou dia ton Iēsoun monon, allʼ hina kai ton Lazaron idōsin hon ēgeiren ek nekrōn.

paragraphs.text: But the chief priests took counsel that they might put Lazarus also to death;
paragraphs.original: ἐβουλεύσαντο δὲ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς ἵνα καὶ τὸν Λάζαρον ἀποκτείνωσιν,
paragraphs.translit: ebouleusanto de hoi archiereis hina kai ton Lazaron apokteinōsin,

paragraphs.text: because that by reason of him many of the Jews went away, and believed on Jesus.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι πολλοὶ διʼ αὐτὸν ὑπῆγον τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ ἐπίστευον εἰς τὸν Ἰησοῦν.
paragraphs.translit: hoti polloi diʼ auton hypēgon tōn Ioudaiōn kai episteuon eis ton Iēsoun.

paragraphs.text: On the morrow a great multitude that had come to the feast, when they heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem,
paragraphs.original: Τῇ ἐπαύριον ὁ ὄχλος πολὺς ὁ ἐλθὼν εἰς τὴν ἑορτήν, ἀκούσαντες ὅτι ἔρχεται ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα,
paragraphs.translit: Tē epaurion ho ochlos polys ho elthōn eis tēn heortēn, akousantes hoti erchetai ho Iēsous eis Hierosolyma,

paragraphs.text: took the branches of the palm trees, and went forth to meet him, and cried out, Hosanna: Blessed [is] he that cometh in the name of the Lord, even the King of Israel.
paragraphs.original: ἔλαβον τὰ βαΐα τῶν φοινίκων καὶ ἐξῆλθον εἰς ὑπάντησιν αὐτῷ, καὶ ἐκραύγαζον· Ὡσαννά, εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίου, καὶ ὁ βασιλεὺς τοῦ Ἰσραήλ.
paragraphs.translit: elabon ta baia tōn phoinikōn kai exēlthon eis hypantēsin autō, kai ekraugazon· Hōsanna, eulogēmenos ho erchomenos en onomati kyriou, kai ho basileus tou Israēl.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus, having found a young ass, sat thereon; as it is written,
paragraphs.original: εὑρὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὀνάριον ἐκάθισεν ἐπʼ αὐτό, καθώς ἐστιν γεγραμμένον·
paragraphs.translit: heurōn de ho Iēsous onarion ekathisen epʼ auto, kathōs estin gegrammenon·

paragraphs.text: Fear not, daughter of Zion: behold, thy King cometh, sitting on an ass`s colt.
paragraphs.original: Μὴ φοβοῦ, θυγάτηρ Σιών· ἰδοὺ ὁ βασιλεύς σου ἔρχεται, καθήμενος ἐπὶ πῶλον ὄνου.
paragraphs.translit: Mē phobou, thygatēr Siōn· idou ho basileus sou erchetai, kathēmenos epi pōlon onou.

paragraphs.text: These things understood not his disciples at the first: but when Jesus was glorified, then remembered they that these things were written of him, and that they had done these things unto him.
paragraphs.original: ταῦτα οὐκ ἔγνωσαν αὐτοῦ οἱ μαθηταὶ τὸ πρῶτον, ἀλλʼ ὅτε ἐδοξάσθη Ἰησοῦς τότε ἐμνήσθησαν ὅτι ταῦτα ἦν ἐπʼ αὐτῷ γεγραμμένα καὶ ταῦτα ἐποίησαν αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: tauta ouk egnōsan autou hoi mathētai to prōton, allʼ hote edoxasthē Iēsous tote emnēsthēsan hoti tauta ēn epʼ autō gegrammena kai tauta epoiēsan autō.

paragraphs.text: The multitude therefore that was with him when he called Lazarus out of the tomb, and raised him from the dead, bare witness.
paragraphs.original: ἐμαρτύρει οὖν ὁ ὄχλος ὁ ὢν μετʼ αὐτοῦ ὅτε τὸν Λάζαρον ἐφώνησεν ἐκ τοῦ μνημείου καὶ ἤγειρεν αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν.
paragraphs.translit: emartyrei oun ho ochlos ho ōn metʼ autou hote ton Lazaron ephōnēsen ek tou mnēmeiou kai ēgeiren auton ek nekrōn.

paragraphs.text: For this cause also the multitude went and met him, for that they heard that he had done this sign.
paragraphs.original: διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ὑπήντησεν αὐτῷ ὁ ὄχλος ὅτι ἤκουσαν τοῦτο αὐτὸν πεποιηκέναι τὸ σημεῖον.
paragraphs.translit: dia touto kai hypēntēsen autō ho ochlos hoti ēkousan touto auton pepoiēkenai to sēmeion.

paragraphs.text: The Pharisees therefore said among themselves, Behold how ye prevail nothing: lo, the world is gone after him.
paragraphs.original: οἱ οὖν Φαρισαῖοι εἶπαν πρὸς ἑαυτούς· Θεωρεῖτε ὅτι οὐκ ὠφελεῖτε οὐδέν· ἴδε ὁ κόσμος ὀπίσω αὐτοῦ ἀπῆλθεν.
paragraphs.translit: hoi oun Pharisaioi eipan pros heautous· Theōreite hoti ouk ōpheleite ouden· ide ho kosmos opisō autou apēlthen.

paragraphs.text: Now there were certain Greeks among those that went up to worship at the feast:
paragraphs.original: Ἦσαν δὲ Ἕλληνές τινες ἐκ τῶν ἀναβαινόντων ἵνα προσκυνήσωσιν ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ·
paragraphs.translit: Ēsan de Hellēnes tines ek tōn anabainontōn hina proskynēsōsin en tē heortē·

paragraphs.text: these therefore came to Philip, who was of Bethsaida of Galilee, and asked him, saying, Sir, we would see Jesus.
paragraphs.original: οὗτοι οὖν προσῆλθον Φιλίππῳ τῷ ἀπὸ Βηθσαϊδὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας, καὶ ἠρώτων αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Κύριε, θέλομεν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἰδεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: houtoi oun prosēlthon Philippō tō apo Bēthsaida tēs Galilaias, kai ērōtōn auton legontes· Kyrie, thelomen ton Iēsoun idein.

paragraphs.text: Philip cometh and telleth Andrew: Andrew cometh, and Philip, and they tell Jesus.
paragraphs.original: ἔρχεται ὁ Φίλιππος καὶ λέγει τῷ Ἀνδρέᾳ· ἔρχεται Ἀνδρέας καὶ Φίλιππος καὶ λέγουσιν τῷ Ἰησοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: erchetai ho Philippos kai legei tō Andrea· erchetai Andreas kai Philippos kai legousin tō Iēsou.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus answereth them, saying, The hour is come, that the Son of man should be glorified.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἀποκρίνεται αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ἐλήλυθεν ἡ ὥρα ἵνα δοξασθῇ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Iēsous apokrinetai autois legōn· Elēlythen hē hōra hina doxasthē ho hyios tou anthrōpou.

paragraphs.text: Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except a grain of wheat fall into the earth and die, it abideth by itself alone; but if it die, it beareth much fruit.
paragraphs.original: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐὰν μὴ ὁ κόκκος τοῦ σίτου πεσὼν εἰς τὴν γῆν ἀποθάνῃ, αὐτὸς μόνος μένει· ἐὰν δὲ ἀποθάνῃ, πολὺν καρπὸν φέρει.
paragraphs.translit: amēn amēn legō hymin, ean mē ho kokkos tou sitou pesōn eis tēn gēn apothanē, autos monos menei· ean de apothanē, polyn karpon pherei.

paragraphs.text: He that loveth his life loseth it; and he that hateth his life in this world shall keep it unto life eternal.
paragraphs.original: ὁ φιλῶν τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἀπολλύει αὐτήν, καὶ ὁ μισῶν τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ τούτῳ εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον φυλάξει αὐτήν.
paragraphs.translit: ho philōn tēn psychēn autou apollyei autēn, kai ho misōn tēn psychēn autou en tō kosmō toutō eis zōēn aiōnion phylaxei autēn.

paragraphs.text: If any man serve me, let him follow me; and where I am, there shall also my servant be: if any man serve me, him will the Father honor.
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν ἐμοί τις διακονῇ ἐμοὶ ἀκολουθείτω, καὶ ὅπου εἰμὶ ἐγὼ ἐκεῖ καὶ ὁ διάκονος ὁ ἐμὸς ἔσται· ἐάν τις ἐμοὶ διακονῇ τιμήσει αὐτὸν ὁ πατήρ.
paragraphs.translit: ean emoi tis diakonē emoi akoloutheitō, kai hopou eimi egō ekei kai ho diakonos ho emos estai· ean tis emoi diakonē timēsei auton ho patēr.

paragraphs.text: Now is my soul troubled; and what shall I say? Father, save me from this hour. But for this cause came I unto this hour.
paragraphs.original: Νῦν ἡ ψυχή μου τετάρακται, καὶ τί εἴπω; πάτερ, σῶσόν με ἐκ τῆς ὥρας ταύτης. ἀλλὰ διὰ τοῦτο ἦλθον εἰς τὴν ὥραν ταύτην.
paragraphs.translit: Nyn hē psychē mou tetaraktai, kai ti eipō; pater, sōson me ek tēs hōras tautēs. alla dia touto ēlthon eis tēn hōran tautēn.

paragraphs.text: Father, glorify thy name. There came therefore a voice out of heaven, [saying], I have both glorified it, and will glorify it again.
paragraphs.original: πάτερ, δόξασόν σου τὸ ὄνομα. ἦλθεν οὖν φωνὴ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ· Καὶ ἐδόξασα καὶ πάλιν δοξάσω.
paragraphs.translit: pater, doxason sou to onoma. ēlthen oun phōnē ek tou ouranou· Kai edoxasa kai palin doxasō.

paragraphs.text: The multitude therefore, that stood by, and heard it, said that it had thundered: others said, An angel hath spoken to him.
paragraphs.original: ὁ οὖν ὄχλος ὁ ἑστὼς καὶ ἀκούσας ἔλεγεν βροντὴν γεγονέναι· ἄλλοι ἔλεγον· Ἄγγελος αὐτῷ λελάληκεν.
paragraphs.translit: ho oun ochlos ho hestōs kai akousas elegen brontēn gegonenai· alloi elegon· Angelos autō lelalēken.

paragraphs.text: Jesus answered and said, This voice hath not come for my sake, but for your sakes.
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν· Οὐ διʼ ἐμὲ ἡ φωνὴ αὕτη γέγονεν ἀλλὰ διʼ ὑμᾶς.
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē Iēsous kai eipen· Ou diʼ eme hē phōnē hautē gegonen alla diʼ hymas.

paragraphs.text: Now is the judgment of this world: now shall the prince of this world be cast out.
paragraphs.original: νῦν κρίσις ἐστὶν τοῦ κόσμου τούτου, νῦν ὁ ἄρχων τοῦ κόσμου τούτου ἐκβληθήσεται ἔξω·
paragraphs.translit: nyn krisis estin tou kosmou toutou, nyn ho archōn tou kosmou toutou ekblēthēsetai exō·

paragraphs.text: And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto myself.
paragraphs.original: κἀγὼ ἐὰν ὑψωθῶ ἐκ τῆς γῆς, πάντας ἑλκύσω πρὸς ἐμαυτόν.
paragraphs.translit: kagō ean hypsōthō ek tēs gēs, pantas helkysō pros emauton.

paragraphs.text: But this he said, signifying by what manner of death he should die.
paragraphs.original: τοῦτο δὲ ἔλεγεν σημαίνων ποίῳ θανάτῳ ἤμελλεν ἀποθνῄσκειν.
paragraphs.translit: touto de elegen sēmainōn poiō thanatō ēmellen apothnēskein.

paragraphs.text: The multitude therefore answered him, We have heard out of the law that the Christ abideth for ever: and how sayest thou, The Son of man must be lifted up? who is this Son of man?
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη οὖν αὐτῷ ὁ ὄχλος· Ἡμεῖς ἠκούσαμεν ἐκ τοῦ νόμου ὅτι ὁ χριστὸς μένει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, καὶ πῶς λέγεις σὺ ὅτι δεῖ ὑψωθῆναι τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου; τίς ἐστιν οὗτος ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου;
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē oun autō ho ochlos· Hēmeis ēkousamen ek tou nomou hoti ho christos menei eis ton aiōna, kai pōs legeis sy hoti dei hypsōthēnai ton hyion tou anthrōpou; tis estin houtos ho hyios tou anthrōpou;

paragraphs.text: Jesus therefore said unto them, Yet a little while is the light among you. Walk while ye have the light, that darkness overtake you not: and he that walketh in the darkness knoweth not whither he goeth.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν οὖν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἔτι μικρὸν χρόνον τὸ φῶς ἐν ὑμῖν ἐστιν. περιπατεῖτε ὡς τὸ φῶς ἔχετε, ἵνα μὴ σκοτία ὑμᾶς καταλάβῃ, καὶ ὁ περιπατῶν ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ οὐκ οἶδεν ποῦ ὑπάγει.
paragraphs.translit: eipen oun autois ho Iēsous· Eti mikron chronon to phōs en hymin estin. peripateite hōs to phōs echete, hina mē skotia hymas katalabē, kai ho peripatōn en tē skotia ouk oiden pou hypagei.

paragraphs.text: While ye have the light, believe on the light, that ye may become sons of light. These things spake Jesus, and he departed and hid himself from them.
paragraphs.original: ὡς τὸ φῶς ἔχετε, πιστεύετε εἰς τὸ φῶς, ἵνα υἱοὶ φωτὸς γένησθε. Ταῦτα ἐλάλησεν Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἀπελθὼν ἐκρύβη ἀπʼ αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: hōs to phōs echete, pisteuete eis to phōs, hina hyioi phōtos genēsthe. Tauta elalēsen Iēsous, kai apelthōn ekrybē apʼ autōn.

paragraphs.text: But though he had done so many signs before them, yet they believed not on him:
paragraphs.original: τοσαῦτα δὲ αὐτοῦ σημεῖα πεποιηκότος ἔμπροσθεν αὐτῶν οὐκ ἐπίστευον εἰς αὐτόν,
paragraphs.translit: tosauta de autou sēmeia pepoiēkotos emprosthen autōn ouk episteuon eis auton,

paragraphs.text: that the word of Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, which he spake, Lord, who hath believed our report? And to whom hath the arm of the Lord been revealed?
paragraphs.original: ἵνα ὁ λόγος Ἠσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου πληρωθῇ ὃν εἶπεν· Κύριε, τίς ἐπίστευσεν τῇ ἀκοῇ ἡμῶν; καὶ ὁ βραχίων κυρίου τίνι ἀπεκαλύφθη;
paragraphs.translit: hina ho logos Ēsaiou tou prophētou plērōthē hon eipen· Kyrie, tis episteusen tē akoē hēmōn; kai ho brachiōn kyriou tini apekalyphthē;

paragraphs.text: For this cause they could not believe, for that Isaiah said again,
paragraphs.original: διὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ἠδύναντο πιστεύειν ὅτι πάλιν εἶπεν Ἠσαΐας·
paragraphs.translit: dia touto ouk ēdynanto pisteuein hoti palin eipen Ēsaias·

paragraphs.text: He hath blinded their eyes, and he hardened their heart; Lest they should see with their eyes, and perceive with their       heart, And should turn, And I should heal them.
paragraphs.original: Τετύφλωκεν αὐτῶν τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς καὶ ἐπώρωσεν αὐτῶν τὴν καρδίαν, ἵνα μὴ ἴδωσιν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς καὶ νοήσωσιν τῇ καρδίᾳ καὶ στραφῶσιν, καὶ ἰάσομαι αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: Tetyphlōken autōn tous ophthalmous kai epōrōsen autōn tēn kardian, hina mē idōsin tois ophthalmois kai noēsōsin tē kardia kai straphōsin, kai iasomai autous.

paragraphs.text: These things said Isaiah, because he saw his glory; and he spake of him.
paragraphs.original: ταῦτα εἶπεν Ἠσαΐας ὅτι εἶδεν τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐλάλησεν περὶ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: tauta eipen Ēsaias hoti eiden tēn doxan autou, kai elalēsen peri autou.

paragraphs.text: Nevertheless even of the rulers many believed on him; but because of the Pharisees they did not confess [it], lest they should be put out of the synagogue:
paragraphs.original: ὅμως μέντοι καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἀρχόντων πολλοὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτόν, ἀλλὰ διὰ τοὺς Φαρισαίους οὐχ ὡμολόγουν ἵνα μὴ ἀποσυνάγωγοι γένωνται,
paragraphs.translit: homōs mentoi kai ek tōn archontōn polloi episteusan eis auton, alla dia tous Pharisaious ouch hōmologoun hina mē aposynagōgoi genōntai,

paragraphs.text: for they loved the glory [that is] of men more than the glory [that is] of God.
paragraphs.original: ἠγάπησαν γὰρ τὴν δόξαν τῶν ἀνθρώπων μᾶλλον ἤπερ τὴν δόξαν τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ēgapēsan gar tēn doxan tōn anthrōpōn mallon ēper tēn doxan tou theou.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus cried and said, He that believeth on me, believeth not on me, but on him that sent me.
paragraphs.original: Ἰησοῦς δὲ ἔκραξεν καὶ εἶπεν· Ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ οὐ πιστεύει εἰς ἐμὲ ἀλλὰ εἰς τὸν πέμψαντά με,
paragraphs.translit: Iēsous de ekraxen kai eipen· Ho pisteuōn eis eme ou pisteuei eis eme alla eis ton pempsanta me,

paragraphs.text: And he that beholdeth me beholdeth him that sent me.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὁ θεωρῶν ἐμὲ θεωρεῖ τὸν πέμψαντά με.
paragraphs.translit: kai ho theōrōn eme theōrei ton pempsanta me.

paragraphs.text: I am come a light into the world, that whosoever believeth on me may not abide in the darkness.
paragraphs.original: ἐγὼ φῶς εἰς τὸν κόσμον ἐλήλυθα, ἵνα πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ μὴ μείνῃ.
paragraphs.translit: egō phōs eis ton kosmon elēlytha, hina pas ho pisteuōn eis eme en tē skotia mē meinē.

paragraphs.text: And if any man hear my sayings, and keep them not, I judge him not: for I came not to judge the world, but to save the world.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐάν τίς μου ἀκούσῃ τῶν ῥημάτων καὶ μὴ φυλάξῃ, ἐγὼ οὐ κρίνω αὐτόν, οὐ γὰρ ἦλθον ἵνα κρίνω τὸν κόσμον ἀλλʼ ἵνα σώσω τὸν κόσμον.
paragraphs.translit: kai ean tis mou akousē tōn rhēmatōn kai mē phylaxē, egō ou krinō auton, ou gar ēlthon hina krinō ton kosmon allʼ hina sōsō ton kosmon.

paragraphs.text: He that rejecteth me, and receiveth not my sayings, hath one that judgeth him: the word that I spake, the same shall judge him in the last day.
paragraphs.original: ὁ ἀθετῶν ἐμὲ καὶ μὴ λαμβάνων τὰ ῥήματά μου ἔχει τὸν κρίνοντα αὐτόν· ὁ λόγος ὃν ἐλάλησα ἐκεῖνος κρινεῖ αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ·
paragraphs.translit: ho athetōn eme kai mē lambanōn ta rhēmata mou echei ton krinonta auton· ho logos hon elalēsa ekeinos krinei auton en tē eschatē hēmera·

paragraphs.text: For I spake not from myself; but the Father that sent me, he hath given me a commandment, what I should say, and what I should speak.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι ἐγὼ ἐξ ἐμαυτοῦ οὐκ ἐλάλησα, ἀλλʼ ὁ πέμψας με πατὴρ αὐτός μοι ἐντολὴν δέδωκεν τί εἴπω καὶ τί λαλήσω.
paragraphs.translit: hoti egō ex emautou ouk elalēsa, allʼ ho pempsas me patēr autos moi entolēn dedōken ti eipō kai ti lalēsō.

paragraphs.text: And I know that his commandment is life eternal: the things therefore which I speak, even as the Father hath said unto me, so I speak.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οἶδα ὅτι ἡ ἐντολὴ αὐτοῦ ζωὴ αἰώνιός ἐστιν. ἃ οὖν ἐγὼ λαλῶ, καθὼς εἴρηκέν μοι ὁ πατήρ, οὕτως λαλῶ.
paragraphs.translit: kai oida hoti hē entolē autou zōē aiōnios estin. ha oun egō lalō, kathōs eirēken moi ho patēr, houtōs lalō.
